Epiphany

ih-PIFF-uh-nee -- four syllables, stress on the second syllable, PIFF. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Epiphany is a moment of sudden insight.

Her epiphany came on the bus: the two data sets had been recorded in different units all along.

Worked Example

For a week the puzzle piece will not fit anywhere. Then, reaching for the salt at dinner, he sees it -- the picture has been upside down on the box the whole time -- and he is out of his chair before the plate stops rattling.

That flash at the dinner table is an epiphany: a moment of sudden insight, arriving all at once and usually while you are thinking about something else entirely. An epiphany is not slow progress; it is the click.

How Epiphany Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

revelation

revelation: a sudden disclosure of something not known before

insight

insight: a clear, deep understanding

breakthrough

breakthrough: a sudden and important discovery

Antonyms

bewilderment

bewilderment: complete confusion

obliviousness

obliviousness: total unawareness

How Strong Is It? — insight → epiphany → revelation

insight vs. epiphany

insight vs. epiphany: Insight can be slow and quiet -- you may build it across a whole semester -- while an epiphany is the single instant in which the understanding lands.

revelation vs. epiphany

revelation vs. epiphany: Revelation is bigger and often comes from outside: a revelation is disclosed TO you, while an epiphany rises inside your own head, usually at the least convenient moment.

Sort It Out

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — epi-

prefix — epi-: upon, on (Greek)

root — phan-

root — phan-: to show, to appear (Greek phainein)

suffix — -y

suffix — -y: state or condition of (Greek -eia)

Put it together

Put it together: Epiphany comes from Greek epiphaneia, 'appearing, manifestation' -- epi- ('upon') plus phainein ('to show'). An epiphany is an understanding that suddenly shows itself upon you, as though it had walked into the room on its own.

Use the root in a new word: phantom

Use the root in a new word: phantom: A phantom of mist drifted across the road and vanished.

Root Check

Word Choice

Epiphany names the moment, not the idea: you have an epiphany, and what you learn in it is the insight. It suits sudden personal understanding -- about a story, a friendship, a problem you had given up on. Capitalized, Epiphany is also a Christian feast day, but the everyday sense is the lightning-flash one.
